chapter: Looking back and the New York years
title: Joining Don Redman's band
summary: After Snub was the last band, Smith had been with Redman and Benny Carter before the war; Redman needed a reed section and sent for him at the Woodside Hotel.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: So after you finished with Snub, which was what...? About a year?
At what stage did you go...? What happened then? What was the next stage after that?
Mmm, let me see. I'm trying to think of what... I was with Don Redman...
You were certainly with Don Redman. I think it was Don Redman before the War started.
Yeah. Don Redman and Benny Carter both. I was both of them before the War started. Snub was the last band I was with.
So in fact, you were with Snub, then, in 1943.
Yes. Uh-huh. In '43. That's right. Yes, because when I left him, I came home and stayed.
Right. So let's talk about Don Redman then. How did you come to join Don Redman's band?

Well, he needed a reed section, and so a lot of the boys hung around... Or most all the musicians hung around the Woodside Hotel anyhow, and they'd come up there, and they knew about me -- somebody told him about me. So he sent for me, and I went down there and started rehearsing down there, in the basement down there at the old ...(?). . . . Down in the basement down there.

So the brass section got to bragging on the reeds; said "You got a good reed section this time, Don." He said, "Well, it'll sound pretty good. It's a little rusty. Maybe it will sound better. Keep rehearsing." So we rehearsed about two or three weeks, and then we went out on the road.
Did you rehearse the reed section?
No. Don rehearsed it. Don didn't let nobody rehearse his band but himself.
